sections.skill: Explain why records and receipts matter and what each record needs

questions.prompt: What is bookkeeping?

choices.text: Choosing which products to put on sale each week
Designing the shelves where the business keeps its books
Writing a business plan for investors once a year
Recording every money event in the business

questions.correct_answer: Recording every money event in the business
questions.intro: BOOKKEEPING is recording every money event in the business: sales, expenses, owner transfers and loans. Each record should show the date, amount, who it was with, and what it was for. A RECEIPT or invoice is the proof. Good records let you see whether you are making money, prepare taxes, answer questions from a tax agency, apply for loans, and catch mistakes or theft. Record transactions soon after they happen; trying to rebuild a year of records from memory is slow and unreliable.

Money

questions.intro: Bookkeeping is like keeping a diary, but only about money. Each entry says when, how much, with whom, and why: "May 3, paid 42 dollars to Paper Plus for boxes." A receipt is like a photo that proves the diary entry is true. If you skip the diary for months, you will not remember what each payment was for, and nobody can check your story.
